issue.description:
Found 2026-08-20 while installing plan-review 2.0. The in-progress lib extraction (uncommitted WIP in plan-author/plan-review/readme-review/spec-review scripts, untracked lib/common.sh) has each script do: source "$(dirname "$0")/../../lib/common.sh". Correct inside the repo, but once a skill is installed to ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/ that path resolves to ~/.claude/lib/common.sh. install.sh copies only the skill directory, so every refactored script fails at its source line with 'No such file or directory' (verified: installed plan-review/scripts/scan-headers.sh exits 1). The parent bead's own spec prescribes that exact path, so the defect is in the spec, not just the WIP.

Options: (a) install.sh also installs lib/ to ~/.claude/skills/lib/ — only works if repo skills and installed skills share the same relative layout; (b) guard the source with an inline fallback — defeats most of the dedup; (c) inline lib/common.sh into each script at install time (a tiny build step in install.sh) — repo stays DRY, installed copies stay self-contained. Recommended: (c). Acceptance: plan-review's SELF-TEST fixture and scan-headers.sh run green from the INSTALLED path, and scripts/check-installed.sh reports no drift.

Until fixed, the installed plan-review carries the HEAD (self-contained) scan-headers.sh and score-plan.sh, so check-installed.sh reports drift on those two files by design.

Verified empirically in a temp HOME in the lib-sourcing world (working tree carrying abeab37c's uncommitted extraction): installed plan-review scan-headers.sh contains the 'Inlined from lib/common.sh during install' block and runs green, and scripts/check-installed.sh exits 0 after install — the bare-cp broken-lib state is flagged (exit 1 naming the path) and cleared by the documented install.sh fix. Dormant at HEAD (lib/ absent, inline_lib_common early-returns; repo scripts are +x and self-contained).

DECISIONS WORTH KEEPING:

1. Read /proc directly, no top/free/vmstat. This renders on every prompt, so it
   is pure bash string work plus a single nproc.

2. MemAvailable, NOT MemFree. MemFree excludes reclaimable page cache and would
   have reported this box as ~95% used while 36G was actually available.
   Cross-checked against `free -g` at write time: script said 25/62G, free said
   total 62 used 25 available 36.

3. Assignment form x=$(( ... )) everywhere, never bare (( ... )). The script runs
   under `set -euo pipefail`, and a bare arithmetic command evaluating to zero
   returns exit status 1 — so the statusline would have blanked itself the moment
   load rounded down to 0%. Verified: load 0.00 renders "0.0/20 0%" and the
   script exits 0.

4. 10# prefix on the fractional part. /proc/loadavg gives two decimals, so a load
   of 0.04 yields the substring "04", which bash arithmetic reads as octal.
   Verified 0.04 -> 0%.

5. Overload is rendered, not clamped: load 41.20 on 20 cores prints 206%, load
   100.00 prints 500%. This box sat at load 21+ (normalized 1.08) earlier the
   same day while NEEDLE refused worker launches for CPU saturation, which is
   exactly the condition the segment exists to make visible. Clamping at 100%
   would hide the difference between "busy" and "wedged".

6. host_ok gates both segments, so an unreadable /proc (container, kernel change)
   drops them rather than blanking the line.

issue.description:
Incident 2026-09-23: the statusline went completely blank. The usage API began returning a third limit (weekly_scoped, Fable) whose resets_at is "2026-09-30T01:00:00+00:00" — no fractional seconds, unlike the other limits ("...59.726900+00:00"). The jq `ts` helper only rewrote ".<digits>+00:00" to "Z", so fromdateiso8601 rejected the string and jq aborted mid-output. `eval "$(jq ... 2>/dev/null)"` swallowed the error, the scoped-limit variables (p7f...) were never set, and `set -euo pipefail` killed the script at the first use ("p7f: unbound variable", exit 1). The harness renders nothing on a non-zero exit.

Immediate fix (already applied live to ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh, NOT yet in this repo): make the fractional part optional in `ts`.

SCOPE of this bead — harden usage-statusline/scripts/usage-statusline.sh so future API/format changes degrade one segment instead of blanking the line:
- Parse the usage JSON defensively: tolerate missing/null/float/string percent, missing or differently formatted resets_at (any fraction, any UTC offset, epoch seconds/ms), missing limit kinds, multiple weekly_scoped limits.
- Quote everything eval'd from jq (@sh); display_name with spaces or metacharacters must not break or inject into eval.
- Isolate each rendered segment so a failure in one cannot kill the rest; always exit 0.
- Host (cpu/ram) and commit segments render even when quota data is unavailable.
- Cache: validate before writing, write atomically (temp + mv), tolerate a corrupt/empty cache.
- Fetch must not block rendering or retry every render on failure; background it with stdio detached.
- Credential refresh must never write a malformed token set (validate the response) and never leave the file world-readable (umask 077).
- Failures are logged to the cache dir so the next diagnosis does not need a repro; a stale cache is visibly marked.
- Add a fixture-based regression test covering the incident shape and the drift cases above.
- Update SKILL.md / README.md / SELF-TEST.md where behaviour they describe changes (e.g. "blank output until first fetch").

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the quota windows mean, the API endpoints, or the token-refresh protocol itself.

Deployment: canonical source is this repo; deploy with ./install.sh usage-statusline, verify with scripts/check-installed.sh usage-statusline.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-23. Canonical source is this repo; deployed with ./install.sh usage-statusline (check-installed.sh: no drift, both the skills-dir copy and the out-of-tree ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh).

AFFECTED PATHS
- usage-statusline/scripts/usage-statusline.sh (rewritten)
- usage-statusline/SELF-TEST.md (cases 1-3 re-pinned; new "Format-drift and failure isolation" block; Expected Behaviors rewritten)

ROOT CAUSE: jq `ts` helper stripped only ".<digits>+00:00"; the Fable weekly_scoped limit arrives as "...T01:00:00+00:00" so fromdateiso8601 aborted, eval "$(jq 2>/dev/null)" hid it, p7f never set, set -u killed the script at line 245 (exit 1 => harness renders nothing). The live one-line hotfix had been applied to ~/.claude/usage-statusline.sh only; this change supersedes it.

DECISIONS
1. Dropped set -euo pipefail (reverses decision 3 of jedscura-a74db3d7; its x=$(( )) assignment form is kept and still harmless). Each segment renders in a subshell instead, because bash aborts the whole command list on an arithmetic error (probed). Always exit 0.
2. No eval. jq emits US-delimited records, `read` splits them. The old eval really executed $(...) in a display_name (reproduced: created a file).
3. Missing/unreadable quota data => `usage n/a` with cpu/ram/git still shown. This DELIBERATELY reverses the old pinned "first run is blank" behaviour (SELF-TEST case 1).
4. Multiple weekly_scoped limits => show the highest percent (was: last one, by accident of jq generator semantics). Unknown kinds ignored. Legacy five_hour/seven_day/seven_day_{opus,sonnet} used if `limits` disappears.
5. Fetch is detached (stdout/stdin closed) and rate-limited to 1 attempt/60s via usage.attempt; previously it blocked rendering up to 8s per prompt when the API was slow, and retried on every render while failing.
6. Cache written atomically after a shape check; a rejected 200 is kept in usage.rejected.json and the last good cache keeps serving (marked `stale <age>` after 15 min).
7. Credentials (found by the new suite, not by the incident): old refresh rewrote .credentials.json at mode 644, wrote null tokens if a 200 had an unexpected body, and put both tokens on curl's argv. Now: umask 077, response validated, compare-and-swap on the refresh token, tokens via stdin/env only. Refresh PROTOCOL itself (endpoint, camelCase body) deliberately unchanged, per this bead's out-of-scope.
8. Regression tests live in SELF-TEST.md (repo convention) and are NOT wired into test-script-fixtures.sh / pre-commit: that suite explicitly scopes usage-statusline out, and CI's skills-validate image may lack jq/flock. Wiring it is a separate, deliberate call.

- The real token-refresh path was not exercised live (token had 19 min left; refresh triggers at <5 min). It is covered only by the stub-curl tests, so the unchanged camelCase request body is still unproven against the real endpoint.
